subject: Renewal: doubling reserved GPU capacity and stepwise throughput guarantees

Subject: Renewal discussion: reserved pool increase and throughput needs

Hi Jordan,

We're starting prep for our October renewal and wanted to flag that we're planning to double our dedicated pool from 16 → 32 GPUs. The main drivers are: a new recommendation pipeline hitting peak traffic in Q1 and a latency-sensitive inference workload for customer-facing features.

A few asks up front so we can align internally:
- Can you provide an updated per-hour reserved rate for 32 GPUs (including any step discounts for staged activation)?
- We'd like a throughput guarantee (p50/p95 token latency) for the new pool and a plan for graceful fallback during capacity pressure.
- Any changes to the contract term or minimum commitment required to secure the 32-GPU pricing?

I've attached our preliminary forecast and would like to schedule a call this week to walk pricing and any operational prerequisites (VPC peering, VPN setup). Procurement is cc'd.

Thanks,
Alyssa Chen
Head of ML Platforms | Hightower AI
Alyssa@hightower.ai

Hi Alyssa — quick technical note ahead of Wednesday's call.

Summary of proposed serving profile for 32‑GPU reserved pool:
- Instance mix: 8 x 4‑GPU nodes (A100-like) with autoscaling headroom for burst.
- Expected sustained throughput: ~3.4M tokens/hour for the pool at our standard batching config.
- Latency SLOs: p50 ~ 40–60ms per token, p95 ~ 180–250ms per token for the same prompt shape you shared. We can tighten p95 by enabling tighter concurrency limits or moving to prewarmed KV cache nodes — this impacts billed reserved hours.
- Fallback behavior: traffic routing to a 16‑GPU warm pool (kept on standby) + host-level soft-limits; when both are saturated, we automatically redirect to a compatible quantized model variant with slightly lower cost and lower VRAM demand.

Operational notes: VPC peering and KMS setup add ~2 business days to the onboarding checklist if keys and network configs are ready.

I'll bring a short benchmarking slide to the call showing p50/p95 for the QPS profile in your forecast.

Thanks,
Dev Patel
Principal PM, Serving Runtime | Redwood Inference

From: marissa_cole@redwood.com
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@hightower.ai>, jordan_blake@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@hightower.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 7 Oct 2026 10:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Renewal ratecard and staged activation options (see attached)

Hi Alyssa — attaching the updated ratecard and a draft SOW for a staged activation plan. Highlights:

- Per-hour reserved pricing (USD):
  • 16‑GPU (current): $18.50/hr per 4‑GPU block (unchanged)
  • 24‑GPU (interim): $17.40/hr per 4‑GPU block (3% blended credit applied)
  • 32‑GPU (full): $16.25/hr per 4‑GPU block (10% discount vs list)
- Staged activation: 0–30 days: warm 16→24 (blended billing), 31–60 days: full 32 (switch to 32‑GPU rate). We can accommodate a one‑time midterm adjustment if forecast changes.
- Throughput guarantee addendum: guaranteed p95 token latency not to exceed 300ms for the configured prompt profile; credits applied for rolling 72‑hour windows where p95 exceeds target and our remediation doesn't meet the rolling SLA.
- Terming options: 12‑month term to get full discount; 9‑month bridge option available at +7% per-hour.

Attachments: Hightower_Renewal_Ratecard_v3.pdf, SOW-doubling-gpu.xlsx

Next steps:
1) Procurement: review SOW and confirm term preference (9 vs 12 months).
2) Technical: confirm model shapes and any KV cache prewarming requests so Dev can finalize the throughput slide.
3) I'll issue a redline-ready contract and a DocuSign link once procurement confirms the term.

Marissa
Marissa Cole
Director of Commercials | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

Thanks team — reviewed the ratecard and SOW. Procurement is inclined toward the 12‑month term to lock the 32‑GPU economics, but we need two clarifications before we sign:

1) The SOW references a p95 credit mechanism — can you clarify the credit cadence and what constitutes "remediation not met"? We need clear thresholds to present to finance.
2) During the staged activation window (days 0–30), will billing reflect actual usage or the warm/reserved commitment? Our CFO wants predictable committed spend during ramp.

If you can reply with those items we can get procurement to e-sign by EOD Tue 10/13. Also please include the DocuSign link when ready.

Best,
Alyssa
